title: Project brief: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Project: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration (PM-482)

Owner(s)
- Product lead: Marissa Cole
- PM (policy semantics/defaults): Paula Mendes
- Program mgmt: Talia Benson
- Eng leads: Ethan Park (Control Plane), Logan Wright (Telemetry/Observability), Chloe Martin (Console Backend)
- SRE stakeholders: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes

Why now / problem statement
Recent rollout regressions have caused elevated latency/5xx for customers while canaries/rollouts were still progressing or while teams were diagnosing signal. Manual rollback is effective but too slow and inconsistent across routes/regions/tiers, especially off-hours. We need the rollout controller to automatically revert traffic to the previous stable model/version when production latency and/or error-rate SLOs breach defined thresholds—while preventing flapping and avoiding “mass rollback storms.”

Goal
- Make Redwood’s rollout controller capable of automatically rolling back a model/version when production latency and/or error-rate SLOs breach configurable thresholds.
- Reduce MTTR and customer impact during bad rollouts (runtime regressions, misconfigurations, capacity/region anomalies), with guardrails against false positives.

In scope
- Rollout Controller integration with SLO monitors (latency + error) via standardized monitor identity + query templates (per route/model/customer tier/region).
- Configurable rollback policies:
  - thresholds (fixed threshold and/or burn-rate; final algorithm per ENG-2314)
  - evaluation windows (short + long window where applicable)
  - minimum traffic requirement / minimum sample size
  - warm-up grace period after starting a rollout step
  - cooldowns to prevent flapping
  - optional “must be worse than baseline” comparison (prior stable)
- Rollback actions:
  - revert canary/A-B traffic split to prior stable version
  - emit audit log + event stream
  - notify Slack/on-call via incident-bot
- Console support:
  - view policy and current health verdict
  - rollback history and reason
  - manual override/ack and pause automation
- Reliability hardening:
  - guardrails for monitoring outages / stale monitors
  - rate limiting to avoid cascading rollbacks across many tenants
- Testing/launch:
  - synthetic SLO breach tests
  - game day
  - staged rollout to internal + low-risk tenants
  - post-launch alert tuning

Out of scope / non-goals
- Building a new monitoring system (we rely on existing telemetry + monitors).
- Auto roll-forward / auto-remediation beyond rollback.
- LLM output quality regressions (covered by separate eval gates).

Target users / customer tiers
- Primary: teams using Rollouts in production (Hosted + Dedicated; Private where rollouts are enabled).
- Priority for v1:
  - Dedicated and enterprise tenants with strict latency SLOs and change-management expectations.
  - High-traffic hosted routes where a regression impacts many end-users.

Success metrics (what we’ll measure)
Product outcomes
- Time to rollback after first sustained SLO breach: p50 < 5 minutes; p90 < 10 minutes (from breach detection to traffic reverted).
- Reduction in customer-visible incident duration for rollout-caused regressions: 30–50% improvement vs baseline quarter.
- % of rollout regressions auto-mitigated (rollback executed) without human intervention: target 60%+ for clear regressions (excluding monitor outage and low-traffic routes).

Reliability / quality of automation
- False-positive rollback rate: <= 1 per 200 rollouts (0.5%) after 4 weeks of tuning; initial launch can be higher with explicit tuning plan.
- “Flapping” rate (rollback triggered more than once per rollout step/tenant due to oscillating monitors): near-zero after cooldown/min-traffic guardrails.
- Monitoring dependency health: monitor fetch success rate > 99.9%; evaluator “unknown verdict” rate tracked and alertable.

Adoption / operability
- 100% of eligible rollouts have a visible policy and verdict in Console.
- On-call runbook usage: all auto-rollback notifications include direct links to dashboard + rollout view + runbook.

Milestones & timeline (6–8 weeks target)
Milestone 0: Alignment & requirements (Week 1)
- Finalize PRD and open questions: defaults, baseline comparison, fail-open vs fail-closed stance.
- Agree on monitor identity contract and minimum required labels.
- Outputs: Confluence PRD, ADR-0147/0148 drafts ready for review.

Milestone 1: Technical design + spike (Week 1–2)
- Validate monitor consumption API, caching strategy, expected query cost.
- Decide evaluation algorithm (burn-rate vs fixed threshold, or hybrid).
- Outputs: Design spec and initial prototype notes.

Milestone 2: Control plane implementation (Week 3–5)
- Monitor client + caching and error handling.
- Policy schema and validation + migrations.
- SLO evaluator module + decision trace logging.
- Rollback executor with idempotency + per-tenant throttling.

Milestone 3: Console + audit + notifications (Week 4–6)
- Console endpoints for verdict/history/policy display.
- Audit log events for policy changes + automated rollback actions.
- incident-bot notifications + Slack routing.

Milestone 4: Testing, game day, and staged rollout (Week 6)
- Synthetic SLO breach harness in CI.
- Game day execution: latency regression, 5xx spike, monitor outage, low-traffic route.
- Fixes and runbook polish.

Milestone 5: GA + tuning (Week 7–8)
- Enable by default for internal canaries.
- Expand cohorts: low-risk hosted routes -> selected Dedicated tenants -> broader.
- Threshold tuning + false-positive review; publish learnings.

Cross-team dependencies / risks
Dependencies
- Telemetry/Observability:
  - Query templates + dashboards/alerts that the controller references.
  - Label consistency across route/model/region/tier.
- Control Plane:
  - Traffic-split revert must be safe, quick, and idempotent.
  - Global rate limiting to avoid cascading rollbacks.
- Console:
  - UX for verdict, reason, history, and manual override/ack.
- SRE:
  - Paging policy (page vs ticket vs notify-only), game day support, on-call runbook.
- Release Eng:
  - Feature flags, staged rollout cohorts, rollback plan for the feature itself.

Primary risks and mitigations
- False positives (low volume, warm-up, correlated incidents)
  - Mitigation: minimum traffic, warm-up grace, baseline comparison option, cooldown, require sustained breach over window(s).
- Monitor outages / staleness
  - Mitigation: explicit “unknown verdict” state, configurable fail-open/fail-closed per tenant/tier, alert on evaluator/monitor fetch errors.
- Rollback storms (many tenants share a region/hardware issue)
  - Mitigation: per-tenant and global throttles; optional dependency on regional incident state; audit + visibility to pause.
- Policy complexity / customer confusion
  - Mitigation: opinionated defaults per tier; Console explains active policy and last decision inputs.

Open questions (to close in PRD/ADR)
1) Evaluation algorithm: burn-rate vs fixed threshold vs hybrid. We need something understandable and safe for v1.
2) Default fail behavior when monitors are unavailable: fail-open (do not rollback) vs fail-closed (rollback) by tier.
3) Baseline comparison semantics: which baseline window, and how to handle baseline being degraded.
4) Dedicated vs Hosted defaults: do we ship different policy presets (min traffic, cooldown) by tier and region.
5) Manual override/ack: what actions are allowed (pause automation for rollout, tenant, or route; duration; audit requirements).

Gating / launch criteria
- Required before cohort expansion beyond internal:
  - Synthetic breach tests passing in CI
  - Game day completed with at least 3 scenarios; action items triaged
  - Audit events verified end-to-end (policy change + auto-rollback trigger + executor action)
  - Runbook finalized and linked in notifications
  - Metrics dashboard exists for: rollbacks executed, unknown verdicts, monitor fetch errors, evaluator lag
